claims.head: Airtight vs. leaky on the kill
claims.body: On the penalty kill, Anaheim is near the top of the league, but San Jose is one of the worst. Penalties are likely to hurt the Sharks more than the Ducks. Anaheim’s penalty kill has been near the bottom of the league for years, though. These two hand each other plenty of power plays, so special teams should get a real say.

stakes: The Ducks go in tied for fourth in the Pacific with 23 points, a point behind the Sharks, third. A regulation win for the Ducks would lift them past the Sharks.

ANA.head: The Ducks have a lot going for them
ANA.body: Even though Anaheim will be without Sennecke, the Ducks have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Sharks’ way back in is getting good looks.

SJS.head: The Sharks have a hill to climb
SJS.body: Even though Anaheim will be without Sennecke, the Ducks have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Sharks can pull it off if they get good looks.

story.head: The Ducks need a win
paras: The Ducks are on a four-game losing streak, and the Sharks (11-13-2) lost 5-2 to Minnesota on Monday. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Sharks third (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Ducks fifth (tied for 22nd). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.

The Sharks’ record (.462) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.406), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Ducks have played better than their record (.460) says: their chances are worth about .520, and losses in one-goal games have held them back.

The Sharks do a lot of their shooting from distance (2nd most), ice the puck a lot (32nd) and have struggled on the power play (32nd). The Ducks give up a lot of dangerous shots (31st) and have had shaky goaltending (30th). Anaheim has allowed 3.80 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. The Ducks are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Sharks. On top of that, both teams like to hit, especially the Ducks (4th), so expect plenty of it.

Macklin Celebrini (10 G / 21 A / 31 P in 24 GP) leads the Sharks in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. For the Ducks, Cutter Gauthier (22 G / 9 A / 31 P in 24 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Mikael Granlund (8 G / 18 A / 26 P in 24 GP) isn’t far behind.
Alex Nedeljkovic (5-3-1 / .901 SV% in 9 GS) is expected to go for San Jose. Laurent Brossoit (4-1-0 / .866 SV% in 5 GS) has struggled for Anaheim so far, but is expected to start.
